assumptions_and_constraints: D1 the payload carries a redacted summary, never raw assistant text, and never tool output, file contents, or diffs.
D2 the summary is heuristic with no model call.
D3 AES-256-GCM end-to-end; the key never leaves the paired devices.
D3b personal Firebase project: Realtime Database plus FCM.
D4 Google sign-in pinned to one account uid on both ends; the Mac refresh token lives in the macOS Keychain.
D5 a session is removed from the database the moment it ends, is archived, or is deleted.
D6 a reply sent while a session is busy is queued and delivered on the next idle event.
D7 remote approval covers flagged tools in enrolled sessions only, with an ask fallback on timeout.
D8 all active sessions publish; no allowlist.
D9 hooks always fail open, with a bounded timeout and exit zero.
D10 push fires on input-needed, finished, and error only.
D11 the Android app is sideloaded as a debug APK over adb.
Mac sign-in uses a loopback-redirect OAuth flow rather than device code, because this machine has a browser.
confirm_before_build: R1: Cloud Functions require the Blaze plan. The alternative is an Android foreground service, trading battery for avoiding an FCM service-account key on the laptop.
Phase 5.1 must prove `claude --bg --resume` continues rather than forks before the reply path is built on it.
risks: R1 — FCM fan-out needs Cloud Functions and therefore billing; the fallback is a foreground service on the handset.
R2 — scope spans hooks, a daemon, a cloud function, and an Android app; phases 1 to 5 deliver a usable subset.
R3 — heuristic summaries read mechanically on list-shaped or question-shaped messages.
R4 — the reply path depends on resume semantics verified from CLI help but not yet exercised end to end.

risks.note: Mechanical fork question answered: resume continues the same session. Context continuity and resume-while-running remain untested because the claude CLI cannot authenticate (OAuth session expired). D6 queue-when-busy stands as the conservative design.

adr_not_needed_because: The decisions are recorded in spec.md and context.md, and the encryption choice is self-evident from the constraint that the host must not be able to read session content.
save_point_commit_policy: One commit per phase. Phases 0 to 2 ship with no remote dependency.

parallel_build_policy.note: Everything outside Phase 1 sequences on shared files or on a prior phase's output.

security_notes: Egress boundary: only a scrubbed summary, a random session id, a timestamp, and an FCM token ever leave the machine; everything else is ciphertext.
nhi7 and nhi5 honoured: no long-lived service-account key on the laptop, and no Admin SDK privilege that would bypass database rules.
AES-GCM is authenticated, so a forged reply cannot be decrypted and is discarded before reaching a session.
Rules pin reads and writes to the signed-in uid; encryption, not the rules, is the confidentiality control.

Cross-uid read and write, root read, out-of-schema subtree, blob-less node, and oversized blob are all denied by the deployed rules, proven live with a valid token and a passing control probe (2026-11-20).
Identity Toolkit error paths no longer echo the request URL, which carried the Web API key as a query parameter.

The pairing QR carries the shared key in the clear by necessity. Exposure is bounded: on request only, 120s display, scrollback wiped, never persisted. Rotation requires typing 'rotate' and unpairs every phone.

Repo is public. Full-history audit before first push: no API keys, OAuth secrets, refresh tokens or private keys in any commit or blob. The real Firebase uid was purged from all 13 commits with filter-branch. Remaining pattern hits are placeholders in config.example.json and redaction test fixtures.

APK distribution open question: google-services.json values (apiKey, projectId, databaseUrl, appId) are compiled into any Android build and are extractable. They are non-secret by Firebase design, but they name the personal project. The shared encryption key is never in the APK; it arrives by QR at pairing and lives in the Android Keystore.
